To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the estimation strategy of quantum process tomography depends upon the matrix elements one selects for estimation and that the information required to estimate any average survival of a quantum channel can be gathered efficiently.
we propose a method to efficiently estimate any parameter of a quantum channel, and we propose a method for efficiently measuring any diagonal element of a chi matrix.

(i) for the estimation of the chi matrix of a quantum process, it is possible to select a set of matrix elements that allows the efficient estimation of any of its parameters with a fixed precision, and (ii) it is possible to efficiently gather all information required to measure any average survival probability.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of estimating a set of parameters that characterize a quantum channel, and we show that it can be solved in a way that is efficient and selective.
the development of new methods for quantum process tomographies that are more efficient than those currently available in the literature.
the efficient estimation of quantum channels and the average survival probabilities of quantum channels.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have found the most efficient way of performing quantum process tomography, in terms of the number of measurements and the number of free parameters to estimate, for a given precision.

the proposed estimation method is efficient and selective, in the sense that it allows one to estimate any of the channel parameters, with fixed precision (and with an average number of measurements which is independent of the dimension of the Hilbert space), by selecting the matrix elements one wants to estimate.

our method provides a way to obtain a complete tomographic characterization of a quantum channel, with a fixed precision, by measuring only a number of matrix elements which is proportional to the number of parameters one wants to estimate.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we present a way to efficiently extract all the information needed to efficiently estimate any of the parameters that characterizes a quantum channel.

, given a quantum process tomography problem, our method allows the user to choose which set of parameters to estimate and to estimate them with fixed precision, with the minimum number of experiments.
we provide a general method for quantum process estimation that is more efficient than the standard method of tomography.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, by selecting an appropriate set of matrix elements, it is possible to obtain a significant improvement over the standard approach.
the estimation of the chi matrix elements can be performed with a number of measurements that scales as the number of elements to estimate, and not as the total number of elements in the chi matrix.
the efficiency of the estimation of the parameters characterizes the efficiency of the process tomography.
